literal: By nature he was mild and did not contend with others, and he never spoke of others' good or ill.
idiomatic: Mild by nature, he shunned rivalry and never spoke of others' virtues or faults.

literal: Once when ill he slept by day and a slave stole from him; Qi Gui feigned sleep and did not see, nor did he reveal it.
idiomatic: Once, ill, he napped by day while a slave stole from him; Qi Gui pretended to sleep, saw nothing, and said nothing.

literal: That slave fled into the Rouran; only then did he laugh and speak of it, yet showed no anger.
idiomatic: The slave later fled to the Rouran; only then did Qi Gui laugh and mention the theft, without a trace of anger.

literal: Late in Xianwen's reign he was made Minister of Guests.
idiomatic: Late in Emperor Xianwen's reign he became Minister of Guests.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaowen he held Eastern Yong Province and was granted Marquis of Yong'an.
idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he governed Eastern Yong Province and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yong'an.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Song, style name Along, loved to aid others in urgent need.
idiomatic: His son Song, styled Along, delighted in helping others through emergencies.

literal: With Wang Zhongxing he was driven from Pingcheng toward Luoyang; the household was poor and could not manage the journey, and Song supplied everything for the road.
idiomatic: Driven from Pingcheng toward Luoyang with Wang Zhongxing, too poor to travel, Song funded their entire journey.

literal: In Emperor Xuanwu's time Zhongxing became a favored intimate and then memorialized to appoint Song as attendant.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu, when Zhongxing won favor at court, he had Song appointed palace attendant.

literal: He requested dredging the Yellow River to open shipping and was made Commandant of Longmen.
idiomatic: He petitioned to dredge the Yellow River for shipping and was made Commandant of Longmen.

literal: After years the work was not completed and he was sentenced to exile.
idiomatic: Years passed without finishing the work, and he was exiled.

literal: When Yuan Ye seized the throne unlawfully he was made Grand Minister of the Imperial Clan.
idiomatic: When Yuan Ye usurped the throne he was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Clan.

literal: His son Taotang ended his career as Court Gentleman for Attendance.
idiomatic: His son Taotang ended his career as Court Gentleman for Attendance.

literal: Wei Guzhen was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Wei Guzhen came from Dai.

literal: When Daowu was in the Helan tribe, He Ranggan sent Hou Yin, Yituo, and others to attempt treason.
idiomatic: While Daowu dwelt with the Helan tribe, He Ranggan sent Hou Yin, Yituo, and others to plot treason.

literal: Guzhen learned of it and secretly sent a swift messenger to report.
idiomatic: Guzhen learned of the plot and sent a secret courier to warn him.

literal: Ranggan suspected Guzhen had leaked the plot, seized and tortured him, pressing his head between two cart axles and injuring one eye.
idiomatic: Ranggan suspected Guzhen had betrayed the plot, seized him, and tortured him by crushing his head between cart axles until he lost an eye.

literal: He did not confess and was then released.
idiomatic: He would not confess and was finally released.

literal: Later, following the pacification of the Central Plains, for merit he was granted Marquis of Dong Province.
idiomatic: After the conquest of the Central Plains he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dong Province for his service.

literal: In early Mingyuan he was General of Soaring Flight and garrisoned Daluo.
idiomatic: Early in Emperor Mingyuan's reign he was General of Soaring Flight and garrisoned Daluo.

literal: He died as Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: He died while serving as Governor of Ding Province.

literal: His son Yiwang inherited.
idiomatic: His son Yiwang inherited the title.

literal: Guzhen's younger brother Nuo was famed for loyalty and prudence.
idiomatic: Guzhen's younger brother Nuo was known for loyalty and discretion.

literal: Following Daowu in the siege of Zhongshan he was first to scale the wall and lost an eye.
idiomatic: In the siege of Zhongshan under Emperor Daowu he was first over the wall and lost an eye.

literal: Daowu sighed and said, "The Nuo brothers have both ruined their eyes to build merit—truly worthy of praise!
idiomatic: Emperor Daowu exclaimed, "Both Nuo brothers have sacrificed an eye for merit—truly praiseworthy!

literal: " He granted him the title of Viscount of Anle.
idiomatic: He enfeoffed him as Viscount of Anle.

literal: Following the pacification of Yao Ping, on return he was made Grand Chieftain of the National Tribes.
idiomatic: After the pacification of Yao Ping he returned and was made Grand Chieftain of the National Tribes.

literal: In Taiwu's time his fief was changed to Duke of Liaoxi.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu his fief was raised to Duke of Liaoxi.

literal: On his death his eighth son Huan inherited.
idiomatic: At his death his eighth son Huan inherited.

literal: Duohou in youth had martial talent.
idiomatic: Duohou showed martial promise in youth.

literal: In Xianwen's time he held provisional authority as Colonel Protecting the Qiang and Rong and General Garrisoning Dunhuang.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianwen he held provisional authority as Colonel Protecting the Qiang and Rong and as garrison general of Dunhuang.

literal: On arrival he requested five thousand light horsemen to enter Khotan in the west, subdue the states together, take supplies from the enemy, and achieve pacification.
idiomatic: On reaching his post he asked for five thousand light cavalry to push into Khotan, subdue the western states, live off the enemy, and pacify the region.

literal: It was not granted.
idiomatic: The request was denied.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaowen he again requested to take Yiwu in the north and cut the Rouran route to the Western Regions.
idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he again asked to seize Yiwu in the north and sever Rouran access to the Western Regions.

literal: The emperor approved the plan but, with eastern works just underway, found it difficult.
idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan but, with major construction in the east under way, could not spare the forces.

literal: He was killed by his wife Yuan.
idiomatic: His wife, of the Yuan clan, murdered him.

literal: Duohou's nephew Qingbin was skilled at mounted archery, had general's stratagem, and was gradually promoted to Grand Palace Counselor.
idiomatic: Duohou's nephew Qingbin excelled at mounted archery, showed a commander's mind, and rose to Grand Palace Counselor.

literal: In Emperor Ming's time the court debated sending the Rouran ruler Anagui back to his country.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming the court debated sending the Rouran ruler Anagui home.

literal: Qingbin memorialized firmly in opposition; they did not follow him.
idiomatic: Qingbin memorialized forcefully against it; the court ignored him.

literal: Later the Rouran indeed seized the acting commander Yuan Fu.
idiomatic: The Rouran later seized the acting commander Yuan Fu.

literal: Qingbin was later made Governor of Si Province.
idiomatic: Qingbin was later appointed Governor of Si Province.

literal: At that time Erzhu Rong's military power grew daily; he once passed through Si Province, and Qingbin detested him and shut the city, refusing entry.
idiomatic: As Erzhu Rong's power grew he once passed through Si Province; Qingbin loathed him and barred the gates.

literal: Rong attacked, seized him, and brought him back to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."
idiomatic: Rong assaulted the city, took him captive, brought him to Xiurong, and mockingly called him "foster father."

literal: Later, through grief, he returned to the capital.
idiomatic: He later returned to the capital in distress.

literal: Soon he was raised as Grand Minister of Splendor and Commander, garrisoning Ruyin.
idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Grand Minister of Splendor and commander garrisoning Ruyin.

literal: On return to court he died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He died after returning to court and was posthumously named Minister of Works.

literal: His son Jin.
idiomatic: His son was Jin.

literal: Jin from youth was quick and perceptive, loved learning, and admired goodness.
idiomatic: Jin was quick-witted from childhood, loved study, and admired worthy conduct.

literal: Because of his surname and family standing he was gradually promoted to Palace Attendant Behind the Throne.
idiomatic: Through his clan name and pedigree he rose to Palace Attendant Behind the Throne.

literal: When Sima Ziru held power, Jin married his niece Lady Pi and thereby was made Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: When Sima Ziru governed, Jin married his niece Lady Pi and was made Secretariat Gentleman.

literal: Later he was made Bureau Director of the Ministry of the Civil Service.
idiomatic: He was later made Bureau Director in the Ministry of the Civil Service.

literal: When Qi Emperor Wenxiang died, Wenxuan ordered Jin at the Northern Palace in Ye, together with Gao Dezheng, to manage secrets.
idiomatic: After Qi Emperor Wenxiang's death, Wenxuan set Jin at Ye's Northern Palace with Gao Dezheng to handle confidential affairs.

literal: In the Tianbao era he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Seven Armies.
idiomatic: During Tianbao he rose repeatedly to Vice Minister of the Seven Armies.

literal: When Xiaozhao assisted in government he was made Minister of the Civil Service.
idiomatic: When Xiaozhao took up regency he became Minister of the Civil Service.

literal: When Wucheng ascended the throne, Zhao Yanshen was originally Ziru's guest and follower; Yuan Wenyao and He Shikai were all old acquaintances of the imperial clan; they jointly recommended him, and his appointments grew heavier.
idiomatic: When Wucheng took the throne, Zhao Yanshen had been Ziru's client, and Yuan Wenyao and He Shikai were childhood friends of the imperial house; together they advanced Jin, and his power deepened.

literal: The Ministry of the Civil Service also controlled appointments, and many matters were secret; thereby he came to hear much of the court's confidential affairs.
idiomatic: As Minister he controlled appointments, many of them secret, and so heard a great deal of the court's inner business.

literal: Later he was Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and died.
idiomatic: He later became Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and died.

literal: Wucheng was then feasting at Santai; Wenyao reported the news, and he at once ordered the music withdrawn and drinking stopped.
idiomatic: Wucheng was feasting at Santai when Wenyao announced Jin's death; he immediately ordered the music stopped and the cups set down.

literal: Outwardly Jin was eminent, yet inwardly his household lacked moral discipline;
idiomatic: Though eminent in public, Jin's household lacked moral discipline;

literal: the inner quarters were foul and mixed, and the world despised him.
idiomatic: his private life was sordid, and the world despised him.

literal: He had a daughter still in the maiden chamber who was suddenly seduced into elopement; Jin then married her to his wife's nephew Pi Yiren.
idiomatic: A daughter still at home was suddenly carried off in elopement; Jin then married her to his wife's nephew Pi Yiren.

literal: Jin also had relations with his widowed sister-in-law Lady Yuan.
idiomatic: Jin also lay with his widowed sister-in-law, Lady Yuan.

literal: Jin once mocked the Bureau Director of the Ministry of the Civil Service, Li Gou of Dunqiu, saying, "Sir, you do not study antiquity."
idiomatic: Jin once mocked Li Gou of Dunqiu, bureau director in the Ministry of the Civil Service, saying, "You never study antiquity."

literal: Gou replied to the clerks, "I truly do not study antiquity—but is bedding one's sister-in-law what you call studying antiquity?"
idiomatic: Gou told the clerks, "It is true I do not study antiquity—but is taking one's sister-in-law what you call antiquity?"

literal: Jin heard it and was greatly ashamed.
idiomatic: Jin heard this and was deeply shamed.

literal: Yet he could also humble himself toward scholars, intending to draw in famous men, but could not distinguish them.
idiomatic: He could still humble himself before scholars and meant to gather famous men, yet could not tell quality from pretense.

literal: There was one Jia Yanshi whose bearing seemed that of a Confucian scholar and who was said fit to serve as envoy to Chen.
idiomatic: One Jia Yanshi looked the part of a Confucian and was said fit to serve as envoy to Chen.

literal: Zuchongru of the Household Bureau of the Minister of Education had insufficient literary polish and eloquence, yet spoke as though unmatched in the age.
idiomatic: Zuchongru of the Minister of Education's household bureau lacked literary polish and eloquence yet talked as if unequaled in the age.

literal: He loved to study the Wu people's lip-quivering and foot-shaking and was laughed at by others.
idiomatic: He imitated Wu performers' lip-trembling and foot-jigging and was mocked for it.

literal: When he saw people he would laugh; contemporaries compared him to the winter cicada.
idiomatic: He laughed at everyone he met; wits compared him to a winter cicada.

literal: He also lacked dignity in youth.
idiomatic: He had little dignity even as a young man.

literal: His son Dezai, beaten with a cattail whip, threw himself into a well.
idiomatic: His son Dezai, flogged with a cattail whip, threw himself into a well.

literal: Jin himself came to the well and called, "Boy, come out!
idiomatic: Jin came to the well himself and shouted, "Boy, come out!

literal: " All who heard laughed.
idiomatic: All who heard burst out laughing.

literal: When his position grew weighty he became very irritable; any bureau director within the ministry who came to discuss business he would at once glare at and revile.
idiomatic: As his power grew he turned furious; any director in his ministry who came to discuss business was met with a glare and a torrent of abuse.

literal: Once he held the great selection he became all the more arrogant and harsh.
idiomatic: Once he controlled appointments he grew still more arrogant and cruel.

literal: The Lady Pi's son Jian, relying on his mother's connection, made many recommendations and took heavy bribes.
idiomatic: Lady Pi's son Jian, trading on the family tie, pushed many candidates and took large bribes.

literal: After Jin's death his younger brother Jing in anger exposed the matter.
idiomatic: After Jin died his younger brother Jing exposed the affair in anger.

literal: Jian was sentenced to two hundred strokes of the rod and assigned to North Ying Province.
idiomatic: Jian was sentenced to two hundred strokes of the rod and sent to North Ying Province.

literal: Earlier, when Jin was envoy to Liang to arrange a marriage, the Liang man Chen Zhao was skilled at physiognomy and told Jin, "Twenty years hence you will be chief minister."
idiomatic: When Jin went to Liang as marriage envoy, Chen Zhao of Liang, skilled in physiognomy, told him, "In twenty years you will be chief minister."

literal: Jin went out and privately told others, "After this gentleman becomes chief minister, within three years he will die."
idiomatic: Jin left and told others privately, "Three years after that man becomes chief minister, he will die."

literal: Zhao later was chief Liang envoy and concurrently Regular Attendant and came to Qi.
idiomatic: Zhao later came to Qi as chief Liang envoy and Regular Attendant.

literal: Jin was then also Right Vice Minister; drums and clarions sounded before him.
idiomatic: Jin was then Right Vice Minister, with drums and clarions before his carriage.

literal: Zhao again told others, "Within two years he will die."
idiomatic: Zhao again told others, "He will die within two years."

literal: It came to pass exactly as he said.
idiomatic: Events proved him right.

literal: Dezai held the post of Regular Attendant of the Palace Gate.
idiomatic: Dezai served as Regular Attendant of the Palace Gate.

literal: Juan's younger brother Diggan was quick-witted and had artistic talent; riding at full gallop he could shoot five targets standing—no one of the time could match him.
idiomatic: Juan's younger brother Diggan was clever and gifted in the arts; galloping, he could hit five standing targets—none could equal him.

literal: In Taiwu's time he was Minister of the Storehouse, added as Regular Attendant, and led the Palace Carriage Attendants.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu he was Minister of the Storehouse, also Regular Attendant, and led the Palace Carriage Attendants.

literal: In serving the throne he was loyal and prudent, and especially skilled at mimicry.
idiomatic: He served the throne with loyal care and excelled at mimicry.

literal: Taiwu, seeing him imitate others' gestures, was so delighted he could not contain himself.
idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu, watching him imitate others' manners, was so delighted he could hardly contain himself.

literal: He was greatly beloved and joined in great plans of state.
idiomatic: He was deeply favored and took part in major state plans.

literal: At that time they were campaigning on the plain and tested battering rams against tombs.
idiomatic: During the campaign on the plain they tested siege engines against tombs.

literal: Diggan was struck by a cable, his ribs broken, and he died.
idiomatic: A cable struck Diggan, broke his ribs, and killed him.

literal: The emperor went in person to mourn with anguish and posthumously made him General of the Central Guard and Duke of Yan Commandery, with posthumous title Hui.
idiomatic: The emperor mourned him in person and posthumously made him General of the Central Guard and Duke of Yan Commandery, with the posthumous title Hui.

literal: His son Changshou held the post of Director of the Right Bureau in the Palace Secretariat, was granted Duke of Kuaiji, and died as Governor of Jing Province.
idiomatic: His son Changshou was Director of the Right Bureau in the Palace Secretariat, enfeoffed Duke of Kuaiji, and died as Governor of Jing Province.

literal: Guzhen's collateral descendant by the sixth generation, Yu, style name Chenxing, was upright by nature.
idiomatic: Guzhen's sixth-generation collateral descendant Yu, styled Chenxing, was stiffly upright.

literal: In Emperor Ming's time he was General of the Martial Guard.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was General of the Martial Guard.

literal: At that time the camp commander Yuan Cha held power; the hundred officials all added respect, but Yu alone made a long bow without kneeling.
idiomatic: When camp commander Yuan Cha held power every official bowed low; Yu alone gave a long bow without kneeling.

literal: Soon he went out as Governor of Cen Province.
idiomatic: He was soon sent out as Governor of Cen Province.

literal: Cen Province's scarlet dye was the finest under Heaven; Cha sent two thousand bolts of white silk to be dyed, and Yu refused to accept them.
idiomatic: Cen Province produced the finest scarlet dye in the realm; Cha sent two thousand bolts of white silk to be dyed, and Yu refused.
